title: Dominant compatible strict henselizations of a normal local domain and a trait
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative normal local domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], with residue field $k$, and let $R$ be a field or discrete valuation ring [def-weil-field, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with residue field $l$. Let $A\to R$ be an injective local ring homomorphism, where local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $R$ is the maximal ideal of $A$. Fix an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and compatible embeddings $k\hookrightarrow l\hookrightarrow\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $k^s$ and $l^s$ be the subfields of $\Omega$ consisting respectively of elements separable algebraic over $k$ and over $l$. Form the strict henselizations $H=A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $B=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ relative to these residue closures [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Then $H$ and $B$ are strictly henselian local normal domains [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Their residue fields identify with $k^s$ and $l^s$. There is a unique local homomorphism $h:H\to B$ extending $A\to R\to B$ and inducing the inclusion $k^s\subseteq l^s$ on residues. The maps $A\to H$, $R\to B$ and $h$ are injective. In particular the induced map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}H$ sends the generic point to the generic point and the closed point to the closed point [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The composite closed geometric points evaluated in $\Omega$ commute with this map. Moreover $\operatorname{Frac}H$ is algebraic over $\operatorname{Frac}A$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure], the two subfields $k^s,l^s$ in the statement are separable closures, since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. They satisfy $k^s\subseteq l^s$: if $x\in k^s$, choose a separable polynomial $f\in k[X]$ vanishing at $x$. A Bezout identity $uf+vf'=1$ remains an identity over $l$, so $f$ remains separable over $l$. Thus $x$ is separable algebraic over $l$, with the specified compatible embeddings.

source.place: Tag 04GU (lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial), compatible residue-closure diagram; elementary Bezout verification of the inclusion.

proof.text: Use the presentations in [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. The pointed etale pairs $(S,\chi:S\to k^s)$ correspond to triples $(S,\mathfrak q,\phi)$ by $\mathfrak q=\ker\chi$ and $\phi:\operatorname{Frac}(S/\mathfrak q)\to k^s$, $a/b\mapsto\chi(a)/\chi(b)$. Conversely compose $S\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ with $\phi$. These operations are inverse on objects and on morphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] at the maximal ideals of $A$ and $R$. It gives filtered etale-algebra presentations of $H,B$, strict henselian local structures, surjections $\psi_H:H\to k^s$, $\psi_B:B\to l^s$ whose kernels are their maximal ideals, and local structure maps $A\to H$, $R\to B$. The residue identifications are induced by these surjections. The universal colimit identifications preserve the structure maps and the pointing maps, so these conclusions apply to the chosen strict henselizations, not just to a different model.

The ring $R$ is a normal domain. This is immediate for a field. For a DVR [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $K_R$ be its fraction field and $v$ its normalized valuation, and let $x\in K_R^\times$. By [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic], $v(1)=v(1\cdot1)=2v(1)$, so $v(1)=0$, and $v(x)+v(x^{-1})=v(1)=0$. Hence $v(x)\ge0$ or $v(x^{-1})\ge0$, and [lem-sc-dvr-nonnegative-valuation-in-ring] gives $x\in R$ or $x^{-1}\in R$. Thus $R$ is a valuation ring, and [lem-weil-pbc-valuation-ring-normal] applies. Now [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] makes every prime localization of each of the normal domains $A,R$ a normal domain. Consequently both are normal rings in the localization sense required for the next step.

source.place: Tag 00IC (lemma-valuation-ring-normal); Tag 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain); DVR as valuation ring, Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr) (1)<=>(2), via the valuation leaves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain] to the two filtered presentations of Step 2. The base rings $A,R$ are domains and normal rings by Step 3, and the colimits are local by Step 2, exactly the hypotheses of that lemma. It follows that $H,B$ are normal domains and that $A\to H$ and $R\to B$ are injective. In particular $A\to R\to B$ is injective by the given injectivity of $A\to R$. Together with Step 2 this proves the asserted strict henselian local normal-domain properties.

source.place: Tag 06DI (lemma-henselization-normal), normality implication, in its etale-colimit form.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] with base ring $A$, target henselian local ring $B$, ind-etale algebra $H$, prime $\mathfrak m_H$, and residue map $\tau:k^s\hookrightarrow l^s$ of Step 1. The preimage of $\mathfrak m_B$ in $A$ is $\mathfrak m_A$: the original $A\to R$ is local and so is $R\to B$ by Step 2. Also $\mathfrak m_H$ lies over $\mathfrak m_A$, and $\tau$ is a $k$-algebra map for the prescribed embeddings. The lemma gives exactly one $A$-algebra map $h:H\to B$ with $h^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_H$ and $\psi_B h=\tau\psi_H$. Thus it is local, extends the specified composite $A\to R\to B$, and has precisely the required residue map. Its uniqueness is among all local extensions inducing this residue inclusion, since every such extension satisfies the two conditions of the cited lemma.

Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$ and $F=\operatorname{Frac}H$, with $K\hookrightarrow F$ from Step 4. Given $z=x/y\in F$ with $x,y\in H$ and $y\ne0$, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] supplies representatives of $x,y$ at stages of the presentation in Step 2. Filteredness puts both at one stage $S$; write them $a,b\in S$. Set $\mathfrak q=\ker(S\to H)$. Since $H$ is a domain, $\mathfrak q$ is prime, and $\mathfrak q\cap A=0$ by injectivity of $A\to H$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable], $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(0)=\kappa(\mathfrak q)/K$ is finite separable. The injection $S/\mathfrak q\to H\to F$ extends to $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to F$ by $a/b\mapsto a/b$, and is a $K$-field embedding. Since $b\notin\mathfrak q$, $z$ is in its image. A polynomial over $K$ annihilating $a/b\in\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ therefore annihilates $z$. Every $z\in F$ is thus algebraic over $K$. Notice that $S\to H$ itself was never assumed injective.

proof.text: In the prime-ideal description of [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}h$ sends a prime to its preimage. Its value at the generic point $(0)$ of the domain $B$ is $\ker h=(0)$, the generic point of the domain $H$. Its value at the closed point $\mathfrak m_B$ is $\mathfrak m_H$ by Step 5. Finally let $\iota_k:k^s\to\Omega$ and $\iota_l:l^s\to\Omega$ be the inclusions. Step 5 gives the actual equality of ring maps $\iota_l\psi_B h=\iota_l\tau\psi_H=\iota_k\psi_H$. Contravariant functoriality of Spec makes this exactly commutativity of the composite closed geometric points. All claims now follow.
